title: Ultrasensitive hybridization capture of short tuberculosis cell-free DNA from urine
author: Amy Oreskovic
materials: Immediately before analysis, thaw urine at 37°C.
Test with Fisherbrand 10-SG Urine Reagent Strips (optional).
If spiking in positive control, add it now.
Amplify in CFX96 Touch Real-Time PCR Detection System (Bio-Rad) with an initial incubation of 94°C for 3 min followed by 45 amplification cycles (94°C for 30s, 64°C for 30s, and 68°C for 1 min).

steps.title: Prepare Collection Tubes
steps.instruction: Prepare 15 mL Eppendorf DNA LoBind tubes containing 500 μL 0.5 M EDTA and 100 μL 1M Tris-HCl pH 8 before urine collection.

steps.title: Collect and Stabilize Urine
steps.instruction: Collect urine in a sterile container and immediately stabilize the sample to protect cfDNA from degradation.

substeps.instruction: Add 10 mL of urine to each prepared 15 mL tube (final concentrations: ~25 mM EDTA and ~10 mM Tris-HCl).
Mix gently by inversion.

steps.title: Isolate Cell-Free Urine
steps.instruction: Remove cell debris from the urine sample.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge urine for 5 minutes at 8000g.
Transfer the cell-free urine supernatant to new 15 mL Eppendorf DNA LoBind tubes.

steps.title: Prepare Streptavidin Beads
steps.instruction: Prepare and wash Dynabeads MyOne Streptavidin C1.

substeps.instruction: Vortex beads for 30 seconds.
Pipette 50 μL (0.5 mg) beads per 10 mL urine sample into a 1.5 mL Eppendorf DNA LoBind tube.

Wash beads three times with an equal volume of high salt wash buffer (1M NaCl, 10 mM Tris-HCl pH 8, 0.05% Tween-20) by placing on a magnetic rack for 1 minute, discarding supernatant, adding buffer, vortexing for 5 seconds, and spinning down briefly.
Resuspend beads in an equal volume of high salt wash buffer (1M NaCl, 10 mM Tris-HCl pH 8, 0.05% Tween-20).

steps.title: Immobilize Capture Probes
steps.instruction: Attach biotinylated capture probes to the streptavidin beads.

substeps.instruction: Pre-mix dual biotinylated capture probes BP1 and BP2 in TLE to a final concentration of 50 μM each.
Add 0.5 μL of the pre-mixed probes (25 pmol of each) per 50 μL beads to the side wall of the bead tube.
Immediately vortex for 5 seconds.
Rotate for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Spin down briefly.
Wash beads three times with an equal volume of high salt wash buffer (1M NaCl, 10 mM Tris-HCl pH 8, 0.05% Tween-20) using the same magnetic rack/vortex/spin method as in the bead preparation step.
Resuspend beads in an equal volume of high salt wash buffer (1M NaCl, 10 mM Tris-HCl pH 8, 0.05% Tween-20).

steps.title: Hybridize TB-specific cfDNA
steps.instruction: Capture target DNA from the urine sample.

substeps.instruction: To each 10 mL sample, add 2.5 mL 5 M NaCl, 127 μL 10% Tween-20, and 50 μL prepared beads (vortex beads well before adding).
Mix well by inversion.
Denature for 15 minutes in a dry bath with a 15 mL tube block preheated to 120°C (urine temp >90°C) or in a 95°C water bath.
Rotate for 30 minutes at room temperature to allow hybridization.
Centrifuge for 5 minutes at 5000g to pellet beads.

steps.title: Wash Captured DNA
steps.instruction: Purify the captured cfDNA from the urine matrix.

substeps.instruction: Remove and discard all but approximately 1 mL of supernatant using a 10 mL serological pipette.
Resuspend beads in the remaining supernatant using a P1000 pipette and transfer to a 1.5 mL Eppendorf DNA LoBind tube.
Place on a magnetic rack for 1 minute and discard supernatant.

Wash twice with 1 mL high salt wash buffer (1 M NaCl, 10 mM Tris-HCl pH 8, 0.05% Tween-20) by inverting 10-20 times (do not vortex), spinning down, and placing on the magnet for 1 minute before discarding supernatant.
Wash once with 1 mL low salt wash buffer (15 mM NaCl, 10 mM Tris-HCl pH 8, no Tween-20) by inverting 10-20 times, spinning down, and placing on the magnet for 1 minute before discarding supernatant.
Place on the magnetic rack and remove as much residual liquid as possible using a P20 pipette.

steps.title: Elute Purified cfDNA
steps.instruction: Release the purified TB-specific cfDNA from the beads.

substeps.instruction: Prepare fresh 20 mM NaOH by adding 400 μL water to 100 μL 100 mM NaOH.
Add 20 μL of the 20 mM NaOH to the beads.
Vortex for 5 seconds and spin down briefly.
Place on a magnetic rack and transfer as much supernatant as possible (usually 20–21 μL) to a PCR well or new DNA LoBind tube.
Partially neutralize the eluate with 3.5 μL 100 mM HCl.

steps.title: Perform PCR Amplification
steps.instruction: Amplify the captured DNA using a specific master mix.

substeps.instruction: Prepare PCR master mix: 1.25 U OneTaq Hot Start DNA Polymerase, 1X NEB OneTaq GC Reaction Buffer (80 mM Tris-SO4, 20 mM (NH4)2SO4, 2 mM MgSO4, 5% glycerol, 5% DMSO, 0.06% IGEPAL CA-630, 0.05% Tween-20, pH 9.2), 0.8 mM dNTPs, 0.4X EvaGreen, 200 nM forward primer, and 200 nM reverse primer.
For experimental samples: Add 26 μL master mix to the entire neutralized output (~24 μL).
For standard curve (0 to 10^5 copies): Add 19 μL nuclease-free water and 26 μL master mix to 5 μL DNA standard.

steps.title: Analyze PCR Results
steps.instruction: Quantify and verify the amplified TB DNA.

substeps.instruction: Measure amplicon Tm via post-amplification melt curve analysis from 65°C to 95°C (0.5°C increments every 5 seconds).
Determine Cq values at a threshold of 500 RFU and calculate recovered copies using the standard curve.
Confirm that the amplicon Tm for clinical samples is ~0.5°C below the positive control Tm.
